title: The Golf Ball Sized Octopus With a Bite You Can't Feel
subject: blue-ringed octopus

scenes.text: This octopus is the size of a golf ball, and you wouldn't even feel its bite.
It's the blue-ringed octopus. At rest it looks plain grey, just a few inches long.
Threatened, it lights up with fifty or sixty bright blue rings. That's the warning.
Its venom is tetrodotoxin, the same nerve toxin as pufferfish. It can paralyze the breathing muscles within minutes.
There's no known antidote. Victims are saved only if someone breathes for them until it wears off.
And the octopus doesn't make the toxin. Bacteria in its saliva glands do.

description:
A blue-ringed octopus is only about the size of a golf ball, yet its tetrodotoxin venom can paralyze breathing muscles in minutes.
The bite is often painless, there is no known antidote, and the toxin is actually made by bacteria living in its salivary glands.
Would you pick up a tiny octopus in a tide pool?
first_comment: The bacteria in its saliva make the toxin, the octopus is immune to it. Which tiny animal would you never touch?
